content.text: Hey,
and/or

Does "in the case that the acl URI in the link header does not exist" mean simply that resourceAcl in this line of FedorLdp.createObject() is null, or does it mean that the URI might have a value but that value points to no resource?
In either case, do we want the method to return immediately with a 409 response code?
What is a "constrainedBy link that indicates the non existence of the URI"? I don't understand what a link that indicates the non-existence of something would be
Thanks!
So I would add the following logic the method that extracts the acl from the link header:
if the resourceAcl points to a non-existent resource return  a 409 indicating problem.
if the resourceAcl points to a resource, but that resource does not contain an  "<> rdf:type <
http://fedora.info/definitions/v4/webac#Acl
>" triple, then return a 409 with an appropriate message that would enable an API user to address the issue.
So yes:  failures should return immediately..
regarding the constrainBy convention: see section 4.2.1.6 of
https://www.w3.org/TR/ldp/
Also for sample constrainedBy examples: you can look at
https://github.com/fcrepo4/fcrepo4/blob/master/fcrepo-webapp/src/main/webapp/static/constraints/NonRDFSourceConstraints.rdf
Also
https://github.com/fcrepo4/fcrepo4/blob/master/fcrepo-http-api/src/main/java/org/fcrepo/http/api/ContentExposingResource.java#L493
Unrelated note: Since this ticket involves two tasks, I would recommend splitting it into two tickets/PRs.
I opened a PR for the first part of FCREPO-2705, namely, "if the resourceAcl points to a non-existent resource return  a 409 indicating problem"
Resolved by
https://github.com/fcrepo4/fcrepo4/commit/069db9f399e2b97c588943af5d417c587ddbbf55
Opened
for second part of this ticket's work.

With the completion of FCREPO-2688,  an ACL can be assigned to a resource based on resource creation (via a PUT or a POST).   The spec indicates that a 400 or 500 series message should returned if the resource does not exist.  If the acl specified in the link does not exist a 400 is returned without a clear explanation in a rel="
http://www.w3.org/ns/ldp#constrainedBy
" link.   See
https://fcrepo.github.io/fcrepo-specification/#link-acl-on-create
There are two tasks to be completed with this jira:
1.  in the case that the acl URI in the link header does not exist,  return a 409 with a constrainedBy  link that indicates the non existence of the URI.
2. if the acl URI exists but does not contain a triple indicating rdf:type of
http://fedora.info/definitions/v4/webac#Acl
(ie  <> a webac:Acl  ) return a 409 with a constrainedBy that indicates the fact that the resource is not correctly typed.
